static_traits.name: Liu Jianmin
static_traits.family_status: Divorced, raising one son and one daughter; caring for grandmother on weekdays.
static_traits.social_status: Has friends and family to talk with, but has not yet discussed dating-related insecurity with them.
static_traits.medical_history: No obvious physical illness; no prior counseling history; no similar problem history.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, Good logic, steady pace, high cooperation; emotions slightly tense and shy, with Self-doubt.

basic_info.main_problem: I worry potential partners will not want to date me because I Has two children; this belief is causing insecurity and doubt in my dating, and making me hesitant and Withdrawal when pursuing new relationships.
basic_info.core_demands: Came to seek counseling because I realized these beliefs hinder me from building new connections; I hope to test and challenge these thoughts and obtain more accurate and balanced views, so as to date with a more confident posture.
growth_experiences: After experiencing Divorce and re-entering the dating scene, the insecurity and doubt of 'being rejected by potential partners because of Has two children' appeared and gradually intensified.

Taking on heavy family caregiving responsibilities: raising one son and one daughter, and caring for grandmother on Work days, needing to constantly weigh and balance personal life and family responsibilities.
Having had several dates where the other's attitude turned cold after mentioning the children; these experiences reinforced the worry and belief that 'having children equals Being rejected'.

core_beliefs: I am not needed enough/not worthy of being chosen (as a partner)
Having children equals burden and will make others reject me

special_situations.event: Thinking about telling a potential partner that I Has two children, or talking about family-related topics
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I reveal that I Has two children, the other will see me as a 'burden' and reject me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Staying defensive and distant early in the relationship, reducing self-disclosure, simply not pursuing the desired person at all
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will reject me for this/no one will want to date me

special_situations.event: Recalling several dating experiences where the other person's attitude turned cold after mentioning children
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A few unsuccessful attempts prove most people are unwilling to date someone with children
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Treats such experiences as a general rule, lowering expectations in advance and avoiding further contact
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As expected everyone is like this; I will be Being rejected

special_situations.event: Others express appreciation for their care of the grandmother and family responsibilities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive feedback is just coincidence and cannot represent the real situation
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Downplaying or negating positive evidence, continuing to judge mainly by negative experiences
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This does not count; it is an isolated case

special_situations.event: Before dating, presets others' views based on 'society's prejudice against people with children'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Society's general view necessarily applies to every person I encounter
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses presumed others' viewpoints to guide action, contracting in advance to avoid embarrassment or rejection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will surely think I have too much baggage

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and build an intimate, stable relationship
core_conflict.fear: Fears being seen as a 'burden', being rejected, and feeling ashamed
defense_goal: Avoiding Being rejected by keeping distance and Withdrawal
Uses the 'social prejudice' explanation to reduce personal vulnerability
Reducing self-disclosure to maintain a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: A potential rejectee carrying a 'burden', a Father who will not be chosen

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked why I do not proactively pursue, or when talking about children/family responsibilities before dating
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes the other party will, as before, view them as a 'burden' and ultimately reject them (transference: projecting past rejection experiences onto the current relationship)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Cautious tone, presetting the other party's negative stance in advance, reducing self-disclosure, and quickly turning to objective statements to avoid going deep into feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor points out positive evidence or encourages reality testing
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing relationship setbacks to the inevitability of 'social bias', thus believing the individual is powerless to change
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using macro and objective discourse (e.g. 'social expectations/bias'), downplaying personal longing and emotional experience, maintaining self-consistency in a steady tone.

manifestations: Returning to dating after Divorce, Withdrawal due to fear of rejection
Unwilling to discuss related unease with friends/family
Feels isolated and embarrassed before and after dates
Balances personal life and dating between raising two children and caring for grandmother on weekdays
Responsibility brings trade-offs and a sense of constraint in choices
outcomes: Reducing outings and dates and postponing new relationships

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: More guarded and less adventurous in dating
Often Self-doubting, shrinking for fear of rejection

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: The impulse to get close and build connection is pressed back into the self, turning into Withdrawal and inaction
Choosing not to pursue people of interest when feeling tense

exception_events.target_problem: In dating situations requiring mentioning children or family responsibilities to a potential partner, the client usually Anticipates rejection and becomes Withdrawal, resulting in reduced interaction or interrupted pursuit.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once, the other person thought caring for grandmother on Work days and taking on family responsibilities was 'very warm', and praised the dedication to family; this differed from past cold experiences and brought a more positive interaction experience.
exception_events.reason: Clue: the other party holds values more recognizing family responsibility; the client truthfully presents their care and sense of responsibility, enabling the other party to see their strengths and give positive feedback.

positive_force: Has a sense of responsibility toward family and has received others' recognition (cared for grandmother, raised two children)
Willing to seek help and do reality testing and behavioral attempts
Has had dating experiences that started smoothly, with a real basis for building connections
Has some capacity for positive self-talk
Has a potential support network of friends and family
negative_force: Mind reading and overgeneralization, amplifying negative experiences
Negating positive evidence and mental filtering, ignoring positive cues
Avoidance and Withdrawal triggered by shame and Fear of rejection
Attributing the predicament to 'social bias', forming Rationalization and a sense of external control

target_behavior.behavior: Withdrawal and avoidance when dating/interacting with potential partners
antecedent: Thinking about revealing that I Has two children
Assuming society's bias against people with children
Recalls past experiences where the other turned cold after children were mentioned
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizes the notion that 'having children = burden', worrying about being rejected because of it and experiencing shame and damaged self-worth
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential rejection and shame, gaining short-term safety and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced initiative and social opportunities, hindered relationship initiation and development, further worsening Loneliness and Self-doubt
